scenes.headline: How Claude Code fences in a shell command
scenes.sub: Anthropic's open-source sandbox runtime, on Linux and macOS
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Rafter! Today: how the sandbox behind Claude Code's shell keeps a command from your files and the internet, with no container.

scenes.text: The kernel's own mounts decide which files a command can see or change, and its only network is a socket to a proxy that checks every host.
scenes.mark: a proxy that checks every host
scenes.say: Mounts decide which files a command can see or change. Its only network is a socket to a proxy that checks every host.

left.title: Ask every time
left.say: Without a sandbox, the agent asks before each command, and people stop reading.

right.title: Draw the boundary once
right.say: With one, the boundary is drawn once, and only a new host asks.

scenes.title: What bubblewrap builds on Linux
scenes.say: On Linux, the policy becomes one bubblewrap command line.

items.say: First, the whole disk is mounted read-only.
Then the project folder is bound back, writable.

items.text: Freeze rc files and git hooks
items.say: Shell startup files and git hooks are frozen again on top.

items.text: Hide secrets under an empty mount
items.say: A denied folder gets an empty mount over it, so its files are gone.
And the network is removed. Only loopback is left.

steps.say: The command's proxy variables point at a small relay inside the sandbox.
The relay forwards into a Unix socket, the only thing that crosses the wall.
On the host, a proxy checks the hostname against the allowlist.
An allowed host gets through. Anything else gets a four oh three, logged against the command.
In Claude Code, writes outside the project and denied hosts fail inside the sandbox.
Its proxies allow known hosts, deny listed ones, and ask you about the rest.

scenes.title: Time to run true, median of 20
scenes.say: On my Linux machine, a wrapped command cost about a tenth of a second with the proxy up. The full command line tool, most of a second.

scenes.text: An allowed domain is a whole domain: the proxy reads hostnames, not what you send there.
scenes.say: An allowed domain is a whole domain. The proxy reads hostnames, not what you send.

recap: No network except the proxy socket
Every host checked against the allowlist
scenes.say: Mounts for files, one socket for the network, and a proxy that checks every host.
